IVX OWNER AI — PRIORITY 0 PRODUCTION RELIABILITY AND 503 RECOVERY

Execute now. Do not return a plan-only response.

CURRENT LIVE FAILURE

The IVX Owner AI backend returned HTTP 503.

This is not an authentication failure.

Observed behavior:

- Owner message was persisted
- Backend AI execution failed
- User received a 503 response
- The request did not automatically recover
- Previous failures also included 60-second and 90-second timeouts
- The system sometimes reports backend health as passing while the Owner AI route is failing

OBJECTIVE

Make the IVX Owner AI reliable under provider failure, backend overload, network interruption and long-running execution.

============================================================
PHASE 1 — IDENTIFY THE EXACT 503 SOURCE
============================================================

Instrument and inspect:

1. Expo client request
2. Render ingress
3. Owner AI API route
4. execution queue
5. AI provider call
6. Supabase persistence
7. response serialization
8. client response handling

For every 503, record:

- trace ID
- task ID
- timestamp
- endpoint
- HTTP method
- status code
- request duration
- queue duration
- provider duration
- Render instance state
- memory and CPU state
- retry count
- exact source of the 503
- exact file, function and line

Distinguish between:

- Render-generated 503
- application-generated 503
- AI provider 503
- gateway 503
- timeout converted into 503
- queue saturation
- restart/cold-start failure

============================================================
PHASE 2 — IMPLEMENT RELIABLE REQUEST MANAGEMENT
============================================================

Add a durable job model:

RECEIVED
→ PERSISTED
→ QUEUED
→ RUNNING
→ WAITING_APPROVAL
→ RETRYING
→ COMPLETED
→ VERIFIED

Terminal states:

VERIFIED
FAILED
BLOCKED
CANCELED

Requirements:

1. Persist every task before execution.
2. Return a task ID immediately.
3. Do not keep the mobile HTTP request open for long-running work.
4. Move long tasks to a background worker.
5. Poll or stream task progress back to the app.
6. Resume incomplete work after Render restart.
7. Prevent duplicate execution with idempotency keys.
8. Preserve the original message and task state after failures.
9. Never lose a task because of a 60- or 90-second client timeout.
10. Do not return contradictory final states.

============================================================
PHASE 3 — RETRY, FAILOVER AND CIRCUIT BREAKER
============================================================

Implement:

- exponential backoff
- jitter
- maximum retry limit
- provider failover
- circuit breaker
- health-based provider selection
- queue backpressure
- concurrency control
- dead-letter queue
- automatic replay of recoverable tasks

Rules:

- Retry only transient failures:
  429, 502, 503, 504, connection reset, timeout
- Do not retry:
  400, 401, 403, invalid input, invalid credentials
- Never retry the same write without idempotency protection
- If the primary provider fails, use the approved fallback provider
- If all providers fail, keep the task queued and notify the owner

============================================================
PHASE 4 — CLIENT EXPERIENCE
============================================================

Replace the current generic failure experience.

The app must show:

- Task received
- Queued
- Running
- Waiting for approval
- Retrying
- Completed
- Failed with exact reason

For HTTP 503:

1. Keep the user message visible.
2. Do not ask the user to retype it.
3. Automatically retry when safe.
4. Show the task ID.
5. Show the last successful checkpoint.
6. Allow manual retry.
7. Allow cancel.
8. Restore progress after app restart.

============================================================
PHASE 5 — HEALTH AND OBSERVABILITY
============================================================

Create separate health checks:

- /health/live
- /health/ready
- /health/ai
- /health/database
- /health/queue
- /health/provider

The service must not report fully healthy when the Owner AI execution route is unavailable.

Add alerts for:

- 503 rate
- timeout rate
- queue depth
- oldest queued task
- provider failure rate
- Render restart
- memory pressure
- CPU saturation
- duplicate execution
- dead-letter tasks

============================================================
PHASE 6 — SUPABASE CONFIGURATION CONSISTENCY
============================================================

Audit the reported missing variables:

- SUPABASE_INSPECTION_DATABASE_URL
- SUPABASE_READONLY_DATABASE_URL
- SUPABASE_DATABASE_URL
- SUPABASE_DB_URL
- DATABASE_URL
- POSTGRES_URL
- SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD

Do not ask for credentials by default.

First:

1. Inspect all existing Render and protected runtime variables.
2. Identify which canonical variable is actually used.
3. Normalize aliases to one validated database configuration.
4. Verify read-only inspection and write-enabled owner-approved operations use the correct connection.
5. Report only the exact missing or invalid variable if runtime proves it is absent or returns 401/403.

============================================================
PHASE 7 — TESTING
============================================================

Run live tests for:

1. Normal chat request
2. 2-minute Senior Developer task
3. 10-minute background task
4. Provider 503
5. Render restart during execution
6. Network interruption
7. App background and reopen
8. Duplicate send
9. Queue congestion
10. Sensitive-action approval
11. Supabase temporary failure
12. Provider failover
13. Dead-letter recovery
14. Retry after 503
15. Owner cancellation

Acceptance criteria:

- no lost messages
- no orphaned tasks
- no duplicate execution
- no contradictory states
- no forced message re-entry
- recoverable 503 tasks complete automatically
- live progress survives app restart
- one final status only

============================================================
PHASE 8 — DEPLOY AND VERIFY
============================================================

If code changes are required:

1. Run typecheck.
2. Run unit tests.
3. Run integration tests.
4. Run production build.
5. Commit to the authorized IVX repository.
6. Push the approved branch.
7. Trigger exactly one Render deployment.
8. Wait for a final deployment state.
9. Verify all health endpoints.
10. Re-run the exact failed request.

Confirm:

GitHub HEAD
=
Render deployed SHA
=
live runtime SHA

============================================================
FINAL EVIDENCE
============================================================

Return exactly one final status:

VERIFIED
FAILED
or BLOCKED

Include:

- root cause of the 503
- whether Render, IVX backend or provider generated it
- task ID
- trace ID
- files changed
- tests run
- GitHub commit SHA
- Render deployment ID
- queue status
- provider status
- retry result
- failover result
- app restart recovery result
- exact failed request re-execution result
- remaining blockers

Do not mark VERIFIED until the exact 503 scenario is reproduced, recovered automatically and completed without losing the owner request.
